title: Impossible to use hotkeys for default screen on surface laptop 4

status.label: Not Actionable
status.detail: Surface Laptop 4 F6/F7 brightness keys show the Windows brightness flyout but reportedly do not change the built-in panel; the report does not identify a PowerToys-controlled action.

next_action.label: No PowerToys change indicated.
next_action.reason: No PowerToys change is indicated unless the reporter demonstrates that applying a Power Display profile/action causes the same internal-panel failure.

judgment.rationale: The report is categorized as Power Display, but the only action described is the laptop firmware/Windows brightness hotkey. No PowerToys setting, profile application or activation is shown. The evidence therefore does not support a PowerToys code fix.
judgment.recommended_action: No PowerToys change is indicated unless the reporter demonstrates that applying a Power Display profile/action causes the same internal-panel failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: The only failing behavior described is the Surface/Windows native brightness-key path; no PowerToys action or profile is shown to be involved. The attached bug report does not establish product causation.

issue_context.summary: Surface Laptop 4 F6/F7 brightness keys show the Windows brightness flyout but reportedly do not change the built-in panel; the report does not identify a PowerToys-controlled action.
known_information: Reporter uses Surface Laptop 4 and Windows 11 25H2.
Native keyboard brightness keys show Windows OSD but do not change panel brightness.
A PowerToys bug-report ZIP is attached.
inferences: The described trigger appears to be the Windows/Surface brightness-key path rather than a Power Display profile operation.
issue_context.analysis: The report is categorized as Power Display, but the only action described is the laptop firmware/Windows brightness hotkey. No PowerToys setting, profile application or activation is shown. The evidence therefore does not support a PowerToys code fix.
initial_investigation: Current PowerDisplay UI is profile-based; the issue describes Surface function keys and Windows OSD, not profile application.
No linked PowerToys fix or duplicate is recorded.
